- **self**: Shard-aware DISTINCT_SCAN prefix eligibility and seek progression (9/1)

## Structure and components

- [statement] For an orphan with a next owned chunk, the skipper preserves the leading index values and shard-key components equal to the boundary, then replaces the remaining contiguous shard-key components with boundary values. Forward chunk-map traversal targets the owned chunk minimum inclusively; backward traversal targets its maximum exclusively at lastShardKeyPos. Index fields after the shard-key block are omitted from that boundary seek. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.0/src/mongo/db/exec/orphan_chunk_skipper.cpp · keywords: Shard-aware DISTINCT_SCAN prefix eligibility and seek progression · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.0/src/mongo/db/exec/orphan_chunk_skipper_test.cpp
- [statement] In r8.2.0, DistinctScan constructs a skipper only when shard filtering is active and fetching is disabled. SERVER-94491 explains that fetching otherwise precedes shard filtering, even if index keys contain shard-key information; merely adding those fields does not enable chunk skipping for a fetching plan. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.0/src/mongo/db/exec/distinct_scan.cpp · keywords: Shard-aware DISTINCT_SCAN prefix eligibility and seek progression · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-94491
- [statement] The r8.2.0 factory requires numeric ordering specifications for matched fields and a consistent product shardKeyDirection * indexDirection * scanDirection across all shard-key components. The product selects forward or backward traversal of the chunk map. Mixed relative directions reject the skipper; hashed matched fields also reject it in this implementation, despite the helper comment describing hashed-ness matching more generally. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.0/src/mongo/db/exec/orphan_chunk_skipper.cpp · keywords: Shard-aware DISTINCT_SCAN prefix eligibility and seek progression · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.0/src/mongo/db/exec/orphan_chunk_skipper_test.cpp

## How it works

- [statement] When no owned chunk remains in the chunk-map scan direction and the shard-key block starts after index position zero, the skipper returns NoMoreOwnedForThisPrefix. DistinctScan frees the orphan and returns NEED_TIME after setting keyPrefix=current key, prefixLen=fieldNo+1, firstExclusive=fieldNo. Exhausting owned shard-key values under one leading index prefix therefore does not terminate the entire distinct scan. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.0/src/mongo/db/exec/distinct_scan.cpp · keywords: Shard-aware DISTINCT_SCAN prefix eligibility and seek progression · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.0/src/mongo/db/exec/orphan_chunk_skipper.cpp, https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.0/src/mongo/db/exec/orphan_chunk_skipper.h

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] In r8.2.0, chunk skipping accepts a contiguous block of shard-key fields inside the index, including after non-shard-key fields. All shard-key components must occur in shard-key order. For example, shard key {b:1,c:1} can match index {a:1,b:1,c:1,d:1}; shard key {a:1,c:1} cannot match index {a:1,b:1,c:1} because its components are separated. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.0/src/mongo/db/exec/orphan_chunk_skipper.cpp · keywords: Shard-aware DISTINCT_SCAN prefix eligibility and seek progression · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.0/src/mongo/db/exec/orphan_chunk_skipper_test.cpp

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] CanSkipOrphans means the skipper has installed a seek point for the next owned chunk boundary. DistinctScan frees the current orphan working-set member, increments orphanChunkSkips, and returns NEED_TIME; the next work call seeks to that boundary rather than returning this orphan or immediately skipping the whole distinct value. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.0/src/mongo/db/exec/distinct_scan.cpp · keywords: Shard-aware DISTINCT_SCAN prefix eligibility and seek progression · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.0/src/mongo/db/exec/orphan_chunk_skipper.h
- [statement] If no owned chunk remains and the contiguous shard-key block starts at index position zero, the skipper returns NoMoreOwned. DistinctScan frees the working-set member, increments orphanChunkSkips, and returns IS_EOF immediately. The terminal return differs from NoMoreOwnedForThisPrefix because later leading non-shard-key prefixes cannot restart the owned shard-key range. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.0/src/mongo/db/exec/distinct_scan.cpp · keywords: Shard-aware DISTINCT_SCAN prefix eligibility and seek progression · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.0/src/mongo/db/exec/orphan_chunk_skipper.cpp, https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.0/src/mongo/db/exec/orphan_chunk_skipper.h
- [statement] Without a usable chunk skipper, an orphan encountered by the shard-filtering distinct executor sets _needsSequentialScan. The next work call uses cursor.next() instead of seek(), preserving the opportunity to find an owned entry with the same distinct value. This fallback increments chunkSkips for each filtered orphan; successful chunk jumps use orphanChunkSkips. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.0/src/mongo/db/exec/distinct_scan.cpp · keywords: Shard-aware DISTINCT_SCAN prefix eligibility and seek progression

## Facts and statements

- [statement] NotOrphan leaves the boundary seek unchanged inside the skipper. DistinctScan then returns the owned entry with ADVANCED and prepares the next distinct seek using keyPrefix=current key, prefixLen=fieldNo+1, and firstExclusive=fieldNo. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.0/src/mongo/db/exec/distinct_scan.cpp · keywords: Shard-aware DISTINCT_SCAN prefix eligibility and seek progression · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.0/src/mongo/db/exec/orphan_chunk_skipper.h
